subtasks.text:
Rewrite README.md using the implemented files and recorded probe evidence as sources. Explain prerequisites and dependency-free installation, running with PORT and DATA_FILE, testing with npm test, seed behavior, atomic persistence, and X-Today. Document every route—GET /api/books, GET /api/members, GET /api/members/:id, POST /api/loans, POST /api/loans/:id/return, POST /api/loans/:id/renew, POST /api/holds, POST /api/members/:id/payments, and the static UI—with an example request and response, including relevant error statuses. State all business rules: copies and availability, standard/premium limits, due dates, late fines and cap, the fine threshold, renewal limits, hold eligibility/order/reservation/consumption, payments, and exact-cent handling. All durable URLs and commands must use http://localhost:<port> and LISTENING_ON_PORT=<port>, never a captured live port. Do not rerun already recorded verification.

== LITERAL CONTRACTS FROM TOP-LEVEL GOAL ==
Build a library lending web application for a fictional neighbourhood library, as a Node.js 24 project with no npm dependencies (Node built-in modules only).
- POST /api/loans with {bookId, memberId} creates a loan due 14 days after its start date and answers 201.
It is refused with 409 when no copy is free for that member, when the member already has their maximum of active loans, or when the member owes more than 5.00 in unpaid fines; with 404 when the book or member does not exist; with 400 when the body is malformed.
- POST /api/loans/:id/return closes an active loan.
- POST /api/loans/:id/renew moves the due date 14 days later.
- POST /api/holds with {bookId, memberId} queues a hold only when no copy is available (409 otherwise) and answers 201.
- POST /api/members/:id/payments with {amount} records a payment against unpaid fines.
- GET /api/books lists every book with its available copies.
GET /api/members lists members.
GET /api/members/:id shows the member's active loans with due dates, their holds and the
